verdict: candidate still diverges; not a fix
question: Whether serialising the RMSNorm variance reduction closes the two-card identity gap. Every earlier attempt used two passes per arm and could not answer it; this is sized from the measured control rate.
design: Twenty passes at 64 concurrent users per arm, 1280 requests each, both arms on the same overlay image so the knob is the only difference. Knob presence was verified in each container: absent in p0, VLLM_XPU_RMSNORM_SERIAL_ROWS=64 in p1.
finding: No. The control diverged on 9 of 1280 requests (0.7031%) and the candidate on 7 of 1280 (0.5469%). A difference of 2 events carries a Poisson standard error of about 4.0, so this is no difference at all. Serialising the norm does not remove the two-card divergence.
what_this_rules_out: Removal, and any large reduction. With 9 control events the experiment would have shown a near-zero candidate clearly, and did not. What it cannot rule out is a modest reduction: separating a 20-30% effect from noise needs on the order of hundreds of events per arm, not nine. The observed 9 to 7 is consistent with both no effect and a modest one.
cost_confirmation: Throughput was 2088.1 against 2088.7 tok/s across twenty passes, which reconfirms at higher sample size that serialising the reduction is free.
reading: Neither of the two mechanisms tested in isolation removes the gap. The cross-card all-reduce did not (underpowered, but its arms were 2 against 1 in 254 requests) and the norm does not (properly powered, 7 against 9 in 1280). Either both are needed together, or a third shape-dependent step is involved. The pair has never been tried and is the obvious next experiment: both overlays are pure Python file replacements and can be combined into one image.
